name: Granada
tagline: The Alhambra, the Albaicín and free tapas
summary: The last Moorish kingdom in Spain, under the Sierra Nevada. Book the Alhambra first, then spend the rest of the time in the hillside lanes of the Albaicín, the cave quarter of Sacromonte and the tapas bars, where a free plate comes with every drink.
seasonNote: July and August pass 38°C; winter is cold at night but clear, with snow on the mountains behind the Alhambra.
arrival: Fast trains from Madrid take about 3 hours 20 minutes; buses from Málaga airport take 1 hour 40 minutes. Granada's small airport has a bus to the cathedral.
gettingAround: The centre is walkable but steep; small C1, C2 and C3 minibuses climb to the Albaicín, Sacromonte and the Alhambra.
cashTip: Cards are accepted almost everywhere; carry coins for the minibuses if you have no card.
foodTip: Order a drink and a tapa arrives free; try remojón salad, habas con jamón and piononos pastries from Santa Fe.
buyTip: Inlaid wooden boxes (taracea), Fajalauza ceramics and lanterns in the Alcaicería market.
baseArea: Near Plaza Nueva, between the cathedral, the Albaicín and the Alhambra

connections.note: Trains via Antequera; buses take about 3 hours.

items.name: Alhambra
items.summary: A Nasrid palace-city of carved stucco, tiled halls and courtyard pools, with the Generalife gardens beside it.
items.expect: Tickets sell out weeks ahead and the Nasrid Palaces entry is at a fixed half-hour; bring your passport.
items.tip: Book on the official site only, take the earliest Nasrid slot, and see the Alcazaba and gardens around it.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult in local currency, not a live ticket quote; check current prices and what is included.
items.sourceNote: Editorial selection. Durations, spending allowances and itinerary advice are planning estimates; check opening days and prices with the venue before you go.
whyVisit: A Nasrid palace-city of carved stucco, tiled halls and courtyard pools, with the Generalife gardens beside it.
The finest Islamic palace in Europe and a UNESCO World Heritage site.
visitFlow: Minibus C3 or walk up through the woods from Plaza Nueva.
Alcazaba, Nasrid Palaces at your slot, then the Generalife.
items.bestFor: Visitors interested in history and context and architecture and design
tradeoffs: Tickets sell out weeks ahead and the Nasrid Palaces entry is at a fixed half-hour; bring your passport.

items.name: Mirador de San Nicolás
items.summary: The square in front of a church with the classic view of the Alhambra against the Sierra Nevada.
items.expect: Packed at sunset with musicians and vendors; watch bags.
items.tip: For a quieter version walk five minutes up to the Mirador de San Cristóbal or Mirador de la Vereda de Enmedio.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult in local currency, not a live ticket quote; check current prices and what is included.

items.name: Albaicín
items.summary: The old Moorish quarter of whitewashed houses, walled gardens (carmenes) and cobbled lanes facing the Alhambra.
items.expect: Steep and confusing; that is half the pleasure.
items.tip: Walk up Carrera del Darro along the river and get lost on purpose, ending at San Nicolás.

items.name: Sacromonte caves
items.summary: A hillside of cave homes where the Roma community developed its own flamenco, the zambra.
items.expect: Evening flamenco in the caves is intimate and touristy in equal measure.
items.tip: Visit the Cuevas del Sacromonte museum by day, and book a show at a small cave venue.

items.name: Royal Chapel and Cathedral
items.summary: The tombs of Ferdinand and Isabella, the monarchs who took Granada in 1492, beside a vast Renaissance cathedral.
items.expect: Two separate tickets; photos are not allowed in the chapel crypt.
items.tip: See the chapel first: Isabella's own art collection is in the sacristy.
